messages:
kevin: Heads-up — I'm sketching a smaller, exchangeable queue adapter interface for the continuous-batching runtime. Goal: let scheduler swap queue implementations (microqueue, slab, coalesce) without changing admission logic. Will paste a proto in a sec.

tyler: curious — what's the primary contract you're trying to preserve?

kevin: Short summary: keep deterministic enqueue semantics (lease vs reject), explicit release, and a compact drain API so the scheduler can form batches without knowing internals. Decouple topology concerns (how batches are formed) from admission and deadline handling.

maria: Can you paste the prototype? high-level makes sense but need to see how headroom / prefetch hints flow.

kevin: ```
// minimal adapter sketch
interface QueueAdapter {
  Enqueue(req) -> LeaseToken | RejectReason
  Release(token)
  Drain(deadline) -> Batch[]
  Stats() -> {depth, inflight, headroom} // opaque numbers for SLOs/telemetry
  // optional hint APIs:
  PrefetchHint?(tenant_id, tokens)
  CanCompact?() -> bool
}
```

sam: RejectReason semantics? backpressure vs early-ack? :thinking:

kevin: Two canonical reject reasons: `REJECT_CAPACITY` and `REJECT_TIMEOUT`. Adapters can surface more, but scheduler must treat capacity as retryable with backoff or route to fallback. Early-ack (accept but drop) should be a distinct flow (e.g., return LeaseToken with special flag).

tyler: If Enqueue returns a LeaseToken with ETA, scheduler can schedule precisely. That helps with p99. Concern: how do we tie LeaseToken lifetime to KV-cache entries so we don't evict prematurely?

maria: also want per-enqueue metadata: origin (streaming vs rpc), token-affinity id, expected sequence length. Those affect batching shape.

kevin: Agreed. Add `meta` to Enqueue: {origin, affinity_id?, seq_len_hint?}. Adapter must propagate affinity to Drain batches. About KV: adapter should expose `ReserveKV(token, bytes)` or at least a headroom number via Stats(). Scheduler uses that to avoid eviction races.

sam: We should define an optional `TryPreempt(token)` so scheduler can attempt to preempt a low-value lease when pressure mounts. Might be tricky but powerful.

kevin: Good call — add `TryPreempt(token) -> PreemptResult` (allowed/denied). Keep it optional; adapters without preempt support just return denied.

tyler: Observability: require adapters emit per-enqueue counters with reason labels, and histogram for enqueue->drain latency. Otherwise rollouts will be blind.

kevin: Yep — mandatory telemetry surface: enqueue_count{reason,origin}, enqueue_latency_ms histogram, drain_batch_size histogram, headroom_gauge.

maria: Migration plan? we can't flip entire fleet at once.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created branch refs/rfcs/exchangeable-queue-adapter and opened draft PR #4127

sam: For rollout, we should have a compatibility shim that implements the new QueueAdapter by wrapping the old queue internals and translating calls. A/B in one region, fail open back to legacy queue on regressions.

kevin: Plan is exactly that. Fallback adapter + feature-flagged scheduler switch. Performance targets: <1% p99 regression, adapter overhead <2ms median on enqueue path.

tyler: One more API thought: expose `CanCompact()` hint so the scheduler/maintenance thread can run compaction safely. That was a pain point in prior refactors.

kevin: Will add `CanCompact()` as an optional API. Also will document ownership semantics: adapter owns internal batch formation; scheduler owns admission and token lifecycle.

maria: tests: add deterministic lease replay test (token replay after node fail) + eviction race sims.

sam: I'll volunteer to run tenant-skew sims + inject heavy small-req traffic.

kevin: Thanks — assigning RFC follow-up to me. I'll update the draft with the extra fields and a migration checklist (shim, telemetry, A/B plan) and post back in ~24h.

maria: Thanks @kevin :thumbsup:

tyler: LGTM as a follow-up RFC.

kevin: Posting proto + simple shim today. Will ping again when PR is ready.
